jobs.title: AI Operations Engineer
jobs.description:
The application window is expected to close on: 10/08/2026

2021485 – AI Operations Engineer (Hybrid)

• This position is listed as hybrid – eligible candidates should expect to be present in the Raleigh-Cisco office on a semi-regular basis.
• Job posting may be removed earlier if the position is filled or if a sufficient number of applications are received.

Meet the Team

Join Cisco’s Commerce Operations Engineering Center (COEC) as an AI Engineer, where you will be part of a dynamic team driving innovation through AI-powered automation. Collaborate with multi-functional AI, engineering, and operations teams to transform sophisticated operational challenges into reliable, scalable AI solutions that advance Cisco’s AI-first future.

Your Impact

As an AI Engineer in COEC, you will design, build, and operate production-ready AI agents that power Cisco’s Commerce Operations. You will translate complex operational needs into automated workflows by orchestrating LLM reasoning, tool/function calling, retrieval, enterprise integrations, and agent-to-agent communication. You will be responsible for the full lifecycle of AI agent delivery—from solution design, guardrails, and system integration to evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement. Your work will help eliminate manual tasks, improve speed and accuracy, and drive operational excellence.

What You’ll Do

• Design and build AI agents that automate manual and repetitive Commerce Operations tasks.
• Implement agent orchestration using frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, or equivalent.
• Build agent-to-agent integrations using emerging standards such as A2A and MCP to enable reliable coordination and delegation.
• Design secure API integrations with commerce platforms and enterprise data sources using REST, GraphQL, webhooks, event-driven services, authentication, rate limiting, and error handling.
• Build and optimize retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines using documents, structured data, and knowledge repositories.
• Implement guardrails, human approval gates, LLM routing, and failover mechanisms to ensure reliability, safety, and cost control.
• Apply prompt and context engineering to ensure AI agents deliver accurate, safe, and consistent outcomes.
• Build evaluation and observability capabilities, including offline test sets, online monitoring, tracing, audit logging, and quality regression detection.
• Own deployment and production operations, including CI/CD, progressive rollout, rollback, monitoring, model/version control, and cost tracking.
• Supervise AI solution performance and report business impact through critical metrics such as efficiency gains, cycle-time reduction, incident reduction, and operational accuracy.
• Continuously improve AI workflows, tools, and methodologies to increase reliability, scalability, and business value.
• Partner with Commerce Operations, application development, infrastructure, and business teams to integrate AI solutions into existing systems and workflows.

Minimum Qualifications

• 7+ years of experience in software engineering or a related field within an enterprise environment.
• Shown experience building and deploying LLM-powered or agentic AI applications in production.
• Strong Python skills and tactical experience with LLM/agent frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenAI SDK, Anthropic SDK, or equivalents.
• Practical expertise in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt engineering, tool/function calling, agent orchestration, and multi-agent communication or workflow orchestration.
• Experience with API and system integrations, including REST, GraphQL, event-driven services, authentication, and enterprise data sources.
• Demonstrated ability to lead technical delivery and collaborate effectively with multi-functional business and engineering teams.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with agent interoperability standards and protocols, including A2A, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and OpenAPI-based tool integration.
• Skilled in designing enterprise-grade multi-agent systems, human-in-the-loop workflows, and implementing agent guardrails.
• Validated experience with agent evaluation and observability tools such as eval harnesses, tracing, LangSmith, Langfuse, or equivalent AgentOps/LLMOps platforms.
• Knowledge of vector databases and sophisticated retrieval methods, including hybrid search, reranking, multimodal retrieval, and knowledge-graph grounding.
• Familiarity with AI governance and safety practices, including RBAC, audit logging, PII handling, and controls for high-risk automated actions.
• Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure) and MLOps/LLMOps practices, including cost-aware LLM routing and FinOps.
• Understanding of commerce platforms, commerce operations, or supply chain operations.
• Consistent record of leading end-to-end AI or agentic AI delivery in sophisticated enterprise environments.
• Advanced degree in AI, Machine Learning, Computer Science, or related field preferred.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

jobs.title: Senior NPI TPM, Ops, Last Mile Delivery & Technology
jobs.description:
Smart Delivery Technologies (SDT) is building the sensing, edge intelligence, and interfaces that make Amazon's delivery network the world's safest and most efficient logistics operation — from the delivery station to the customer's doorstep. Our portfolio includes real-time hazard detection, guidance systems for drivers and associates, environmental data capture, and edge compute devices.

We are looking for a Senior New Product Introduction (NPI) Technical Program Manager (TPM), Operations to lead new products end-to-end at the intersection of engineering, supply chain, and operations.  This role requires someone who can drive cross-functional execution while also going deep on build and sourcing strategy, supplier negotiations, and cost structure.

The ideal candidate has a strong background in Operations Program Management (OPM), is comfortable owning supplier sourcing decisions, and can build and defend detailed costing breakdowns (BOM cost, tooling, NRE, landed cost) that inform business decisions. You will partner with engineering, product, finance, procurement, and manufacturing teams to launch new products on time, at target cost, and at the right quality bar.

Because SDT lives inside an operations org, our timelines are tight and we must justify product value through pilots before progressing toward mass production. The right person embraces this tension: applying the rigor of a high-volume NPI process while pragmatically right-sizing it to an operations-driven, pilot-to-production reality. This is a high-visibility role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, dives deep into data, and is equally comfortable in a supplier negotiation, a design review, or a business review with senior leadership.  Travel should be expected up to 25-30% of the time to engage with suppliers and contract manufacturers globally for builds and relationship development.

Key job responsibilities
* Own the end-to-end NPI program plan across multiple concurrent product launches, from design freeze through mass production ramp
* Drive OPM rigor: schedules, milestones, risk registers, and readiness reviews across engineering, supply chain, quality, and manufacturing
* Lead supplier sourcing strategy, including RFQs, supplier selection, and negotiations in partnership with procurement
* Own material availability across multiple programs by partnering with key component suppliers, manufacturing partners, and product owners to proactively drive sourcing activities and risk buy authorizations
* Build and maintain detailed costing breakdowns (component-level BOM cost, tooling/NRE, labor, overhead, landed cost) and identify cost-reduction opportunities
* Monitor and proactively manage component and product-level End of Life (EOL)
* Partner with finance to align program costs against business case targets and flag variances early
* Identify, track, and resolve program risks and blockers; escalate trade-offs to leadership with clear data-backed recommendations
* Drive design-for-cost and design-for-manufacturability discussions with engineering teams
* Plan and execute pilots/POCs that justify product value, and translate pilot results into go/no-go decisions and the path toward mass production
* Create and present program status, cost, and sourcing updates to senior leadership on a regular cadence
* Establish and improve NPI processes, tools, and mechanisms to scale program management across the organization

- Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science or equivalent
- 6+ years of technical program management experience

- Experience in written and verbal communication with the ability to present complex technical information in a clear and concise manner to executives and non-technical leaders
- Experience managing global supply chains and contract manufacturer (CM/ODM) relationships
- Hands-on experience building and analyzing costing breakdowns (BOM cost, tooling/NRE, landed cost)
- Experience managing cross-functional programs involving engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing, shipping multiple products from concept to mass production

Global Clinical Product Leader, Immunology

Make a more meaningful contribution. Impact patients’ lives every day.

Join a place with the commitment, knowledge and backing from the business to continue expanding our pipeline. With one of the broadest and deepest pipelines, we are determined to keep contributing and pushing forward. When we get it right there’s nothing more motivating.

AZ’s vision is to grow and expand the indications and assets in immunology to become a major player in the field. This Global Clinical Program Lead (GCPL) role in Late stage clinical development in Immunology is designed to help deliver on that ambition.

The role - Global Clinical Program Lead, Immunology

As GCPL in Gastroenterology, you will provide medical and scientific input into programs of small molecules, biologics or cell therapy for clinical stage assets and provide program leadership that is passionate about gastroenterology and clinical immunology. You will take responsibility for clinical development in cross-functional teams to support early to late phase clinical development activities. These include the creation of overall clinical development plans and clinical study design, writing study concepts and protocols, key study and health authority documentation, medical monitoring and ensuring timely delivery of studies.

In this role, you will be:

• Responsible for study design concept delivery
• Responsible for driving clinical and scientific decisions within Global Study Team remits together with other team members
• Accountable for clinical, scientific, and ethical components of studies including patient safety on a study and/or program level in compliance with Good Clinical Practice
• Accountable for scientific medical input to all relevant study documents (including and not limited to protocol, statistical analysis plan, amendments, informed consent, case report forms, safety, and risk-based monitoring plans) to ensure consistency within clinical program and alignment with scientific rationale.
• Accountable for scientific medical content at international investigator meetings, and support to local Marketing Companies (MC) for country level activities
• Accountable for safety surveillance on a study level and/or program level including the process for Adverse Events (AE)/ Serious AE reporting.
• Reviews (with the GCH) the Clinical Study Report and plays key role in preparation and production of relevant sections (Introduction, Results, Discussion).
• Accountable for induction and education of new Global Study Team members.
• Work with GCH and TA leadership for identifying risks and proposing mitigation strategies to deliver successful phase IIb, III, IV or Life Cycle Management studies
• Delivering clinical, scientific, and medical information/query responses to Regulatory Agencies, Ethic Committees, Marketing Companies (MCs), and investigators/sites, and provides clarifications as well as solves clinical, scientific, and medical issues in the Global Study Team

Leadership:

• Clinical representative on indication in Global and Clinical Product Teams and/or sub-teams
• Lead governance interactions in conjunction with or as delegated by the GCH such as DRACs, DRCs, PRCs
• Co-lead the study and program strategy for publication development and approval of publications with the GCH
• Line management of project study physicians and scientists

Basic Qualifications

• Medical degree (MD or MD-PhD) required, with specialist training or experience in gastroenterology/gastrointestinal diseases and/or clinical immunology
• Minimum of 5 years in pharma industry, with experience in leading clinical trials to support approval (Phase 2-4)
• Knowledge of biostatistics, global regulatory environment, and pharmacovigilance relevant to the role
• Experience in leading or reviewing a clinical program to support an indication: design, clinical development plan and Target Product Profile.
• Good presentation skills and effective communication with internal and external collaborators
• Knowledge and experience to work across projects, with a fast-learning curve when moving into new disease areas

JOB SUMMARY

Work independently or assist test engineer to Lead and administer Test technicians and Debug technicians for a specific workcell. Also to maintain proper record of all machine preventive, maintenance work for ISO requirement. Responsible for new projects/equipment set up commission to achieve the company/WC goal.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

·         Exhibit proficiency in the use of electronic test and measurement equipment.

·         Frequent customer interface, including travel to customer sites for advanced diagnostic issues.
·         Prepare daily reports and recommend solutions to technical problems as required.
·         Perform preventative maintenance program to reduce down time and increase process yields to achieve departmental goals.
·         May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.
·         Enable to conduct test process in conjunction with the customer: In Circuit Test, Software download, Functional Test, extended tests - Burn In, HASS, Soak Testing, ESS, X-Ray.
·         To lead and guide a group of test technicians for supporting production lines.
·         To ensure all test equipment are maintained to the best condition for minimum downtime
·         To interface with vendors and supplies for machine maintenance and calibration.
·         To manage a good level of machine spares parts to ensure minimum production impact due to machine downtime.
·         To set up the test equipment for new projects or new businesses.
·         To provide cost reduction through automation and process simplification.

·         Participates in meetings, seminars and training sessions to stay appraised on new developments.

·         Review all test processes and identify any untested components.
·         Shall supply comprehensive and accurate documentation for all testers, component programmers and debug / repair processes.
·         Contribute to the improvement of test yields, test efficiency, tester intermittence, electrical defects and overall tester development.
·         Shall contribute to the training of Test Technicians, Debug Technician, Debug Operator, Test Operators and Component programmers.
·         Investigate new and existing test and diagnosis methods to improve existing products and support advancing technologies.
·         Ensure controls are in place to conform to ISO standards.
·         Train and lead the Debug Technicians / Debug Operator to analysis the fault of the production line.
·         To trouble shoot and analysis the unit unable repair by Debug Technician.

JOB QUALIFICATIONS

·         Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers, and the general public.
·         Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.

jobs.title: DR Delivery Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Kyndryl, we design, build, manage and modernize the mission-critical technology systems that the world depends on every day. So why work at Kyndryl? We are always moving forward – always pushing ourselves to go further in our efforts to build a more equitable, inclusive world for our employees, our customers and our communities.

The Role

Your Role

Join our team as a Delivery Manager and embark on an exciting professional journey that goes beyond just delivering services. In this role, you will be accountable for the overall leadership, governance, and delivery of Data Protection, Disaster Recovery (DR), Backup & Recovery, and Cybersecurity Services for a major enterprise environment. As a crucial member of our organization, you will forge powerful and enduring business-to-business relationships with our customers, acting as a trusted advisor to senior executives and guiding cross-functional teams to ensure mission-critical systems remain resilient, secure, and continuously available.

In this role, you won't simply be a passive participant; you'll be at the forefront, leading the enterprise Disaster Recovery and resiliency program. You will oversee operational readiness, recovery testing, and remediation plans, and serve as the primary leadership authority during major incidents, critical recovery events, and high-pressure situations. By partnering closely with architecture, engineering, cybersecurity, and operations teams, you will champion automation, modernize existing capabilities, and steer transformation initiatives that enhance our customer's cyber resilience posture.

Moreover, your impact extends beyond day-to-day operational execution. As a Delivery Manager, you will be entrusted with customer governance and the financial stewardship of multi-million-dollar contractual commitments. You will establish and direct executive governance forums, manage budgets and resource forecasts, protect recurring revenue streams, and ensure contractual commitments, service levels, and regulatory requirements are consistently met or exceeded.

At Kyndryl, we foster an environment of innovation, collaboration, and growth. As a Delivery Manager, you will lead and mentor a dynamic, geographically distributed team of technical specialists across infrastructure, storage, backup, and cyber recovery disciplines. You will have access to cutting-edge resources, comprehensive support, and professional development opportunities that enable you to continuously expand your technical and leadership acumen.

If you're ready to embrace a role that challenges you intellectually and empowers you to make a meaningful impact on the stability and security of enterprise infrastructure, join us as a Delivery Manager and become an integral part of Kyndryl's journey.

Your Future at Kyndryl

Kyndryl has a global footprint, which means that as a Delivery Manager at Kyndryl you will have opportunities to work on projects and collaborate with colleagues from around the world. This role is dynamic and influential - offering a wide range of professional and personal growth opportunities that you won't find anywhere else.

Key Responsibilities

• Provide overall leadership and governance for Data Protection, Disaster Recovery, Backup & Recovery, and Cybersecurity Services.
• Lead the Disaster Recovery and resiliency program, including operational readiness, DR planning, testing/exercises, recovery capabilities, remediation, and executive governance.
• Oversee day-to-day service delivery and ensure performance against contractual commitments, SLAs, security requirements, compliance obligations, and customer expectations.
• Establish strong governance with customer leadership, including executive reviews, service performance, risks, issues, priorities, and improvement plans.
• Serve as the primary leadership point of contact for major incidents, escalations, service risks, and critical recovery events.
• Lead cross-functional technical and delivery teams across storage, backup, recovery, infrastructure, security, resiliency, and related service areas.
• Develop and manage budgets, forecasts, resource plans, utilization, and overall financial performance.
• Identify operational and delivery risks and ensure appropriate mitigation, ownership, and executive visibility.
• Drive continuous service improvement, including problem management, process improvement, automation, standardization, and operational efficiency.
• Lead strategic projects and transformation initiatives that improve resilience, recoverability, cybersecurity posture, and service quality.
• Partner with architecture, engineering, operations, security, and customer teams to introduce new capabilities and modernize existing services.
• Identify opportunities for automation, innovation, and new service capabilities that improve customer outcomes and business value.
• Develop strong relationships with customer executives and key stakeholders and act as a trusted advisor on resiliency, recovery, and service-delivery strategy.

Kyndryl currently does not require employees to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19, however, if you are hired to work at a client, customer, or partner location, you may be required to show proof of vaccination to align with their respective COVID-19 vaccination policies.  Those who believe they are eligible may apply for a medical or religious accommodation prior to the start of employment.

Who You Are

Required Experience & Skills

• Strong experience leading large-scale infrastructure or managed-services delivery in a complex enterprise environment.
• Direct Disaster Recovery and resiliency experience, including DR planning, testing, recovery execution, governance, and continuous improvement.
• Experience with Data Protection, Backup & Recovery, storage, and infrastructure technologies.
• Working knowledge of cybersecurity operations, security controls, risk management, and regulatory/compliance requirements.
• Demonstrated experience managing customer relationships and executive-level governance.
• Strong program and project management capabilities with experience managing multiple concurrent initiatives.
• Experience managing financial performance, budgets, resource planning, and service-delivery commitments.
• Strong understanding of ITIL/service management disciplines, including incident, problem, change, and service-level management.
• Ability to lead geographically distributed, cross-functional technical teams.
• Strong communication, executive presentation, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills.
• Proven ability to operate effectively during major incidents and high-pressure recovery situations.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting a large healthcare or highly regulated enterprise environment.
• Experience with enterprise DR, cyber recovery, backup and storage platforms.
• Experience driving automation, operational transformation, and continuous improvement.
• Relevant certifications in areas such as PMP, ITIL, Disaster Recovery/Business Continuity, cybersecurity, cloud, or infrastructure technologies.

The compensation range for the position in the U.S. is -
$156,360 to $296,880based on a full-time schedule.

Your actual compensation may vary depending on your geography, job-related skills and experience.  For part time roles, the compensation will be adjusted appropriately. The pay or salary range will not be below any applicable state, city or local minimum wage requirement.

California (All Other):$171,960 to $326,520

Massachusetts$156,360 to $326,520

New York City: $187,560 to $356,280

Washington: $171,960 to $326,520

Washington DC:$171,960 to $326,520

This position will be eligible for Kyndryl’s discretionary annual bonus program, based on performance and subject to the terms of Kyndryl’s applicable plans. You may also receive a comprehensive benefits package which includes medical and dental coverage, disability, retirement benefits, paid leave, and paid time off.  Note: If this is a sales commission eligible role, you will be eligible to participate in a sales commission plan in lieu of the annual discretionary bonus program.
Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis.

Equal Opportunity Employer

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

Being You

Diversity is a whole lot more than what we look like or where we come from, it’s how we think and who we are. We welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. But we’re not doing it single-handily: Our Kyndryl Inclusion Networks are only one of many ways we create a workplace where all Kyndryls can find and provide support and advice. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you – and everyone next to you – the ability to bring your whole self to work, individually and collectively, and support the activation of our equitable culture. That’s the Kyndryl Way.

What You Can Expect

With state-of-the-art resources and Fortune 100 clients, every day is an opportunity to innovate, build new capabilities, new relationships, new processes, and new value. Kyndryl cares about your well-being and prides itself on offering benefits that give you choice, reflect the diversity of our employees and support you and your family through the moments that matter – wherever you are in your life journey. Our employee learning programs give you access to the best learning in the industry to receive certifications, including Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Skillsoft, and many more. Through our company-wide volunteering and giving platform, you can donate, start fundraisers, volunteer, and search over 2 million non-profit organizations.  At Kyndryl, we invest heavily in you, we want you to succeed so that together, we will all succeed.

Get Referred!
If you know someone that works at Kyndryl, when asked ‘How Did You Hear About Us’ during the application process, select ‘Employee Referral’ and enter your contact's Kyndryl email address.

Job title: Finance Business Partner – Tours Site

• Location: Tours, France

About the job

As Finance Business Partner for Tours Site within our Manufacturing & Supply Finance team, you'll deliver strategic financial insights and partner with operational leaders to drive performance at one of Sanofi's key manufacturing sites. Ready to get started?

Built in 1967, our Tours pharmaceutical production facility is one of the leading industrial enterprises in Indre-et-Loire. With over 300 employees, each year, Tours produces over 3.5 billion tablets and capsules for France and the world, serving cardiovascular disease, central nervous system disorders, and hypercholesterolemia. With 93% of production destined for international export (Europe, United States, Japan, Australia), Tours is at the heart of France's pharmaceutical sovereignty and innovation.

About Sanofi:

We're an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people's lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. jobs.title: FSP - Scientist: Immunology
jobs.description:
Work Schedule

Standard (Mon-Fri)

Environmental Conditions

Adherence to all Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) Safety Standards, Laboratory Setting, Some degree of PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) required (safety glasses, gowning, gloves, lab coat, ear plugs etc.)

Job Description

This is a fully onsite role based at our customer’s site in San Diego, CA (Carmel Valley area). We welcome applicants from all locations within the US. Please note that relocation assistance is not provided for this position, and any relocation costs will be the responsibility of the candidate.

Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.

Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life - enabling our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while taking science a step beyond through research, development and delivery of life-changing therapies. With clinical trials conducted in 100+ countries and ongoing development of novel frameworks for clinical research through our PPD clinical research portfolio, our work spans laboratory, digital and decentralized clinical trial services. Your determination to deliver quality and accuracy will improve health outcomes that people and communities depend on – now and in the future.

Thermo Fisher's clinical research business is a leading global contract research organization and world leader in serving science. We are passionate, deliberate, and driven by our mission – to enable our customers to make the world healthier, safer, and cleaner.

Our Laboratories Functional Service Partnership (FSP) team plays a direct role in advancing drug development by creating sustained groups of talent within our customers’ organizations to provide long-term support. Through this collaborative approach, our professionals bring their commitment to excellence, industry knowledge, and operational strength directly into customer environments, helping to enhance capabilities and advance the delivery of life-changing therapies.

As part of the Immunology Research Team, the individual will contribute to the assessment of novel therapeutic approaches to target autoimmunity and inflammation. We are seeking a highly motivated, dedicated and collaborative scientist with knowledge and expertise in cellular and molecular immunology, with experience in antibody/small molecule drug discovery. The successful candidate will work as part of a highly team-oriented and collaborative group. The focus of this position will be to support the progression of multiple drug discovery projects in the immunology space, by independently designing, performing, and validating key in vitro cell-based functional assays. The candidate will also perform experiments to understand the mechanism of action of drug candidates, and present data to cross-functional teams.

Key responsibilities:

• Designing and performing experiments to support scientific activities and project goals.
• Separation of human PBMC from whole blood, as well as the isolation of primary human leukocyte populations for downstream assays.
• Isolation of immune cells from murine organs (spleen, etc).
• Maintain cell lines and primary cell cultures.
• Perform immunological assays including lymphocyte proliferation, activation, cytokine secretion, and differentiation.
• Perform basic molecular biology assays including mRNA isolation, Taqman qPCR, NanoString.
• Flow cytometric analysis of immune cell subsets and analysis of data.
• Perform immunoassays (MSD, ELISA, etc) for analysis of soluble proteins in cell supernatants/murine plasma.
• Maintains and updates SOPs and electronic lab notebook, and writes data summaries for experiments conducted.
• Present data and findings to cross-functional project teams.
• Provides training and/or supervision to junior staff, as needed.
• Other duties as assigned.

Education and Experience:

• Bachelor's degree in lab sciences such as Chemistry, Biochemistry, Material Science, Immunology, Biology, Molecular Biology or similar
• Scientist: Previous experience that provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the job (comparable to 2+ years’)
• Or a Masters

In some cases, an equivalency, consisting of a combination of appropriate education, training and/or directly related experience, will be considered sufficient for an individual to meet the requirements of the role.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

• Experience with human PBMC isolation and cellular subset purification.
• Expertise in cell culture and aseptic technique, involving both immortalized cell lines and primary human/murine cells.
• Experience in immunoassays (ELISA, MSD, Western Blot, etc) and molecular biology techniques (mRNA isolation, qPCR).
• Experience with multicolor flow cytometric analysis, including spectral cytometry, is a plus.
• Able to explain the process behind data generated and the implications of the results.
• Strong knowledge of one or more scientific disciplines, especially immunology.
• Strong knowledge of scientific principles, methods, and techniques, and demonstrated ability to work with a variety of laboratory equipment/tools.
• Excellent communication, problem-solving, and analytical thinking skills.
• Ability to work as part of a cross-functional team, and present data and concepts clearly and concisely.
• Demonstrated ability to meet multiple deadlines with a high degree of accuracy and efficiency, and experience prioritizing multiple projects is a plus.

Working Environment:

Below is listed the working environment/requirements for this role:

Able to communicate, receive, and understand information and ideas with diverse groups of people in a comprehensible and reasonable manner.

Able to work upright and stationary and/or standing for typical working hours.

Able to lift and move objects up to 25 pounds

Able to work in non-traditional work environments.

Able to use and learn standard office equipment and technology with

proficiency.

May have exposure to potentially hazardous elements, including infectious agents, typically found in healthcare or laboratory environments.

Able to perform successfully under pressure while prioritizing and handling multiple projects or activities.

Benefits

We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus, healthcare, and a range of employee benefits. Thermo Fisher Scientific offers employment with an innovative, forward-thinking organization, and outstanding career and development prospects. We offer an exciting company culture that stands for integrity, intensity, involvement, and innovation!

Compensation and Benefits

The hourly pay range estimated for this position based in California is $31.00–$40.00.

This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:

• A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs
• Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement
• At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy
• Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan
• Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount

For more information on our benefits, please visit:  https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards

jobs.description:

Job Description:

TK Maxx jest częścią grupy TJX Europe, w której znajdziesz różne produkty, ale łączy nas ta sama cecha – poszukiwanie skarbów, które dają nam radość. Od stylowych perełek, znanych marek do unikatowej biżuterii, gwarantujemy naszym klientom szalone możliwości każdego dnia. Równie dynamiczna jest nasza praca. W sklepach nieustannie coś się dzieje, co sprzyja rozwojowi i zaangażowaniu. Każdy dzień daje możliwość odkrycia czegoś nowego.

Dołącz do naszego zespołu na stanowisku: Sprzedawcy / Sprzedawczyni

Zatrudnienie w niepełnym wymiarze godzin,

praca tymczasowa, na okres wzmożonego ruchu do końca grudnia 2026r.

Stawka wynagrodzenia na tym stanowisku wynosi 28,64 zł brutto za godzinę.

Jest to jednolita stawka wynagrodzenia dla wszystkich pracowników zatrudnionych na tym stanowisku w tej lokalizacji.

Szukasz pracy, dzięki której zajdziesz daleko?

Osoba na tym stanowisku reprezentuje naszą markę, dlatego powinna być pewna siebie i komunikatywna. Wyobraź sobie pracę, w której nie ma dwóch takich samych dni. W sklepach nieustannie coś się dzieje – w jednej chwili obsługujesz klienta, a za moment rozpakowujesz dostawę pełną nowych niesamowitych produktów.

Stając się częścią rodziny TK Maxx, dołączasz do zespołu świetnych ludzi – a to dopiero początek korzyści. Oferujemy szeroki pakiet benefitów wspierających zdrowie i dobre samopoczucie, w tym:

• Więcej urlopu na start
• Prywatną opiekę medyczną
• Ubezpieczenie na życie
• Dofinansowanie do karty MultiSport
• PPK
• Program nagród za staż pracy
• Zniżki pracownicze na zakupy w TK Maxx

Odkryj to, co nas wyróżnia w TK Maxx – przekonasz się, że to coś więcej niż praca. Jesteśmy dynamiczną organizacją, razem współpracujemy, uczymy się i rozwijamy. Dołączając do naszego zespołu w sklepach, możesz liczyć na pełne wsparcie różnorodnej i zgranej grupy.

Masz prawo wiedzieć, jakie informacje o Tobie posiadamy i w jaki sposób wykorzystujemy te informacje. W celu uzyskania bardziej szczegółowych informacji na temat wykorzystywania przez nas danych i praktyk ich udostępniania, prosimy odwiedzić: mytjx.com/mytjx/Global_TJX_Privacy_Notice.pdf i zapoznać się z naszą pełną Polityką Prywatności. W Spółce obowiązuje polityka ochrony sygnalistów.

Jesteśmy pracodawcą równych szans. Zachęcamy do aplikowania wszystkie osoby, w szczególności bez względu na wiek, poziom sprawności, tożsamość płciową, stan cywilny, ciążę lub macierzyństwo, przynależność związkową, pochodzenie etniczne, narodowość, kolor skóry, religię, wyznanie, przekonania polityczne, orientację seksualną.

Job Description:

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other.  We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

Help Build the Future of Caterpillar

At Caterpillar, technology always has a purpose, which is to solve our customers’ toughest challenges. Through Cat Technology, we are solving problems by building the intelligence layer that connects machines, data, and people to make jobsites safer, more productive, and more sustainable. By combining deep domain expertise in physical systems with software, connectivity, autonomy, and AI, we deliver solutions that work in the real world—on real jobsites, at global scale.

You’ll build and deploy against one of the most unique data foundations—over 1.6 million connected assets generating real-world data daily.  These data and platform capabilities are enabling the development of AI models, edge computing architectures, and software systems that scale across fleets, products, and industries. The result will be a new generation of machines that continuously learn, improve, and deliver performance at scale.

Be Part of What’s Next in Autonomous Construction Sites

Construction autonomy is one of the most complex challenges in applied AI, and at Caterpillar, advancements in physical AI, simulation, sensing, and edge computing are turning things that once felt impossible—intelligent machines operating in dynamic jobsites—into reality.

Our connected ecosystem brings together massive volumes of high-quality data to create a foundation where engineers like you can build and deploy against.

If this work motivates you, we invite you to join our team. In these roles, you’ll work at the intersection of the physical and digital worlds. You’ll help design and deliver intelligent systems that enable machines to perceive their environment, make informed decisions, and support safer, more productive operations.

Apply today to build the new era of construction autonomy at Caterpillar.

Job Summary:

The CI Portfolio Analyst turns fragmented program, roadmap, delivery, partner, supplier, customer-learning, and technical-review information into a coherent cross-program view for Atlas and the broader CI portfolio. This role maintains portfolio intelligence, synthesizes interactions and consequences across programs, develops scenarios and trend analysis, and prepares decision-ready roadmap and executive artifacts. The CI Portfolio Analyst supports the Senior Manager, Portfolio Management and Deputy Portfolio Manager by making cross-program implications visible without replacing authoritative source systems or assuming execution ownership that belongs to Product, TPMs, Mission Leads, Architecture, Engineering, Finance, Procurement, partners, or the RTE.

What You Will Do:

• Maintain the cross-program CI portfolio view, including active, planned, proposed, paused, stopped, and unresolved work, with clear source, ownership, milestone, and evidence context.
• Synthesize portfolio roadmaps across Atlas and the broader CI remit, identifying program interactions, sequencing implications, shared capabilities, dependencies, gaps, and decision points.
• Prepare concise executive portfolio artifacts that translate complex roadmap, delivery, capacity, risk, dependency, partner, supplier, and customer-learning information into clear implications and decisions.
• Produce portfolio scenarios, trend analysis, and decision-impact views to support prioritization and start-stop-continue-defer recommendations.
• Analyze how partner, supplier, procurement, customer-learning, demonstration, and technical-review outcomes affect portfolio milestones, roadmap choices, risks, and executive commitments.
• Support integrated roadmap governance by maintaining traceability among Objectives, Customer Market Requirements, Epics, Features, Milestones, dependencies, baselines, forecasts, evidence, and controlled changes.
• Help drive Intake alignment on value, capacity, affordability, and cross-program consequence analysis for incoming demand and portfolio tradeoffs.
• Identify conflicting, incomplete, stale, or unsupported portfolio claims and preserve source differences until accountable owners resolve them.
• Develop reusable analytical methods and portfolio to improve the consistency, traceability, and usefulness of executive reporting.
• Support leadership reviews with clear fact patterns, options, consequences, open assumptions, and recommended areas for decision or deeper validation.

What You Will Have:

• Planning: Tactical and Strategic: Knowledge of effective planning techniques and the ability to connect near-term program activity with multi-year roadmaps, milestones, dependencies, capacity, and business objectives.
• Program and Portfolio Analysis: Ability to organize and interpret information across multiple complex digital programs, technical domains, workstreams, and source systems.
• Decision Making and Critical Thinking: Ability to evaluate incomplete or conflicting information, distinguish fact from assumption, identify consequences, and frame decision-relevant options.
• Data Analysis and Reporting: Ability to synthesize qualitative and quantitative information into credible trends, scenarios, executive insights, and fit-for-purpose reporting products.
• Project and Portfolio Management: Knowledge of roadmap, milestone, dependency, RAID, change-control, governance, and benefits or value concepts used across complex portfolios.
• Stakeholder Management: Ability to work across Product, Engineering, Architecture, Finance, Procurement, suppliers, partners, and program leadership without direct authority.
• Written and Visual Communication: Ability to produce concise, structured, traceable, and executive-ready narratives, roadmaps, tables, and presentation materials.
• Organizational and Systems Thinking: Ability to recognize interactions across programs and control surfaces, identify downstream effects, and avoid creating duplicate or disconnected reporting systems.

Top Candidates Will Have:

• Experience performing portfolio, program, strategy, roadmap, business, or decision-support analysis across multiple technical programs or interdependent workstreams.
• Demonstrated ability to synthesize roadmap, milestone, capacity, risk, dependency, partner, supplier, and delivery information into clear cross-program implications.
• Experience preparing executive portfolio reviews, scenarios, recommendations, and visual artifacts that support decisions rather than only summarize status.
• Ability to preserve traceability to authoritative sources while identifying inconsistencies, gaps, assumptions, and unresolved ownership.
• Experience with digital, autonomy, AI, connected-machine, software/platform, industrial technology, or similarly complex technical environments.
• Working knowledge of Azure DevOps, Power BI, Microsoft Project, Excel, PowerPoint, Confluence, PPM, or comparable planning and reporting tools.
• Experience with roadmap synthesis, portfolio trend analysis, prioritization scenarios, partner or supplier consequence analysis, or customer-learning integration.
• Strong analytical judgment, attention to detail, written communication, and the ability to move comfortably between working-team evidence and executive-level implications.
• Ability to operate within clear accountability boundaries: the analyst integrates and interprets evidence but does not manufacture status, approve technical content, own source data, or operate the integrated execution plan.

Additional Details:

• This position requires the candidate to work full-time onsite at the Irving, TX office (Dallas)
• Domestic relocation assistance is available for this position.
• Visa sponsorship is NOT available for this position

$128,470.00 - $192,710.00

jobs.description:
Position Summary...

What you'll do...

2027 Summer Intern: Load Logistics Manager, Transportation
What You’ll Do...
About Walmart Supply Chain: End-to-End (E2E) Delivery
As part of the E2E Delivery organization, you will contribute to the success of the Walmart Supply Chain! Sam Walton founded our company with the belief that the customer is #1. It is not just a belief, but our way of doing business. With our E2E Delivery Team at the forefront of retail transformation, you can work on a team that is ultimately focused on delighting our customers, saving them both time and money in unexpected ways. As the biggest player in the game, we trust our associates to innovate the future of supply chain & transportation!

About our Teams:
Transportation - The Transportation team implements business processes and improvement strategies to stay current on supply chain and replenishment processes and procedures. As the largest grocer, ensuring our stores have items like food on hand and delivering it to our customers to feed their families is an important role. This is among many ways the team makes a difference in times of need, including helping provide Emergency relief during National Emergencies.

About Our Program:
Each summer, we select the best and brightest to look under the hood of the world’s largest retailer at our Walmart across multiple locations. During the 11-week program, our interns work directly with teams who are changing the way the world shops. This is the beginning of what could be an exciting career with Walmart!

The intern experience includes:

• An impactful individual project designed to align to your skillsets and interests
• Direct access to leadership across the enterprise
• Executive-led speaker sessions with insightful Q&A
• Community outreach events
• Networking and social events
• Learning & development opportunities targeting both hard and soft skills
• Deep dives into different areas of our business
• Time management and leadership development as a full-time associate
• Compensation and housing assistance provided

Roles and Responsibilities:
We are looking for a friendly and proactive Logistics Load Manager Interns to join our team! As a Logistics Load Manager Intern, you will be responsible for assisting in the operation of multiple departments and performing various job-related responsibilities and duties throughout the facility as needed.
How you’ll spend your day as a Load Logistics Manager Intern…

• Communicate efficiently with customers, suppliers, and associates both verbally and in writing.
• Maintain quality and safety standards by training associates on logistics and company policies.
• Monitor and manage productivity by preparing, reviewing, and analyzing business reports.
• Dispatch drivers while complying with Department of Transportation regulations.
• Identify and resolve concerns of associates, customers, and suppliers.
• Implement business plans to meet facility goals related to production, quality, and safety.

Why you’re a great fit:

• If you can focus on meeting internal and external customer needs.
• If you can demonstrate professional judgment by making informed decisions based on data.
• If you can align activities with organizational goals and use existing processes to achieve performance objectives.
• If you can ensure high-quality transportation operations by adhering to company policies.
• If you can form trusting and collaborative relationships across the organization.
• If you can show creativity and strength in the face of change and obstacles.
• If you can model ethical behavior and enforce compliance with policies.
• If you can develop logical and convincing arguments in support of initiatives.
• If you can develop plans to achieve organizational goals and improve processes.

Office Environment: You will be placed in one of our Transportation Command Centers.

U.S. Hub Locations: Bentonville, AR and Grove City, OH.
*Location availability is limited based on job profile and business needs.
Desired Majors: Supply Chain Management, Transportation and Logistics, Operations, Business, Economics, Finance, Mathematics, Engineering, or other relevant majors

• Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program currently
• Expected graduation date between December 2027-August 2028
• IMMIGRATION SPONSORSHIP IS NOT AVAILABLE FOR THIS ROLE

Are you ready to be at the forefront of patient care and make a impact in your community? As a Staff Pharmacist at Walmart, you will be empowered to share your clinical knowledge and work to the top of your license. This is a great opportunity for those who love talking to patients and advocating for their wellbeing.

Our pharmacy team operates in an energetic environment equipped with the resources and technology needed to succeed. We are dedicated to providing quality, heartfelt care to our patients and ensuring their health and wellness. This role is crucial in helping us achieve our goals and make a difference in the community.

• Counsel customers regarding healthcare and prescription medication needs.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Pharmacovigilance Operations
jobs.description:
Associate Director, Pharmacovigilance Operations

Nurix Therapeutics is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of targeted protein degradation medicines, the next frontier in innovative drug design aimed at improving treatment options for patients with cancer and inflammatory diseases. Powered by a fully AI-integrated discovery engine capable of tackling any protein class, and coupled with unparalleled ligase expertise, Nurix’s dedicated team has built a formidable advantage in translating the science of targeted protein degradation into clinical advancements. Nurix aims to establish degrader-based treatments at the forefront of patient care, writing medicine’s next chapter with a new script to outmatch disease.

Position:

The Associate Director, Pharmacovigilance Operations (PVO) is responsible for all PV operational and compliance aspects of assigned Nurix products across the product lifecycle — from First-In-Human (FIH) studies through post-marketing — and for oversight of the end-to-end management of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs).
This role serves as the PVO lead for assigned products, driving in-stream quality review, regulatory submission oversight, retrospective quality review, and reconciliation activities, while partnering cross-functionally with Clinical Operations, Data Management, and Regulatory Affairs. The role also provides vendor oversight, supports audit and inspection readiness, and contributes to the development of PV infrastructure, systems, and processes.

Responsibilities:

PV Operations for Clinical Study Management
•    Serve as the PVO Lead for assigned products, representing PV operations in cross-functional clinical team meetings.
•    Support SAE reconciliation activities in partnership with Clinical Operations and Data Management.
•    Track and manage Reference Safety Information (RSI) updates and ensure timely dissemination across study teams and systems.
•    Contribute to the safety content of clinical study documents, including Study Protocols, Informed Consent Forms (ICFs), Clinical Study Reports (CSRs), Investigator Brochures (IB)/RSI, and other relevant study documentation.
•    Maintain accountability for the data integrity of safety data outputs from the Safety Database for aggregate reports, Health Authority requests, and other safety requirements.
•    Manage the drug safety mailbox.
ICSR Management & Case Processing Oversight
•    Own end-to-end ICSR management, including in-stream quality review, regulatory submission oversight, and retrospective quality review to ensure timeliness, accuracy, and compliance with global regulations.
•    Generate reports and listings/line-listings (LLs) from the Global Safety Database (GSDB) to support SAE reconciliation, Analysis of Similar Events (AOSE), Safety Signal Assessment Reports, and Aggregate Safety Reports (ASRs).
•    Monitor case processing metrics and drive resolution of quality or timeliness issues.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
•    Partner closely with Clinical Operations, Data Management, Regulatory Affairs, and Medical Safety to ensure alignment on safety data flow, reconciliation, and reporting timelines.
•    Act as a key liaison between PV and other functions for assigned products throughout the product lifecycle.

Vendor Oversight

•    Provide oversight of outsourced PV activities and vendors, establishing and monitoring key quality and compliance metrics (KPIs/KQIs).
•    Ensure vendor performance aligns with contractual, quality, and regulatory expectations; drive corrective actions as needed.
•    Support management of PV Agreements/Safety Data Exchange Agreements (SDEAs) with license partners.
Audits, Inspections & Compliance
•    Participate in and support internal audits, regulatory inspections, and associated CAPA development and tracking.
•    Build and maintain PV infrastructure, systems, and processes to ensure inspection readiness and launch readiness in compliance with global PV regulations and guidelines (e.g., FDA, EMA, ICH).
•    Develop and maintain PV operations and compliance related SOPs and work instructions.
Strategic & Departmental Contributions
•    Develop short- and long-term goals for the PVO function in alignment with broader departmental and organizational objectives.
•    Lead or contribute to PVO-related initiatives, process improvements, and system implementations as assigned.
•    Perform other duties as required.

Requirements:

Education & Experience

•    Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Nursing, or a related field required; advanced degree (PharmD, MS, PhD) preferred.
•    Minimum of 8–10 years of pharmacovigilance/drug safety experience, including significant experience in PV operations, ICSR management, and clinical safety support.
•    Prior experience managing or overseeing PV vendors/CROs required.
•    Experience with managing PV budget and invoicing.
•    Experience supporting regulatory inspections and audits (FDA, EMA, or other health authorities) strongly preferred.
•    Experience across the full product lifecycle (clinical development through post-marketing) preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

•    Strong working knowledge of global PV regulations and guidelines (21 CFR, EU GVP, ICH E2 series, GVP Modules).
•    Hands-on experience with Global Safety Databases (e.g., Argus Safety, or equivalent) and case processing/reporting workflows.
•    Demonstrated experience with SAE reconciliation, RSI tracking, and aggregate safety reporting.
•    Strong vendor management skills, including KPI/KQI development and performance oversight.
•    Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with Clinical Operations, Data Management, Regulatory, and Medical Safety teams.
•    Strong analytical, organizational, and project management skills; able to manage multiple products/priorities simultaneously.
•    Experience authoring or contributing to SOPs, work instructions, and PV process documentation.
•    Detail-oriented with a strong quality and compliance mindset; experience preparing for and supporting inspections/audits.

Salary Range:  $229,500 - $255,867

Location:    Onsite - Brisbane, California

Fit with Nurix Culture and Values
•    Strong team orientation; highly collaborative
•    Solutions and results-oriented focus
•    Hands-on approach; resourceful and open to diverse points of view

jobs.title: Founding Brand & Communications Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT MESHY

Meshy is building the generative AI layer for 3D. Developers, creators, game studios, and enterprise teams use Meshy to turn ideas into production-ready 3D assets in minutes instead of weeks. We’re a Silicon Valley company with a global team, growing fast, and now at the point where the category we’re creating needs a name, a story, and a voice.




WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Today, Meshy is known as a very good AI 3D tool. That’s not enough. The next phase requires Meshy to be understood as a company with a defined category position, a long-term vision, and real cultural weight in AI and creative software.

You’ll be the person who answers these questions and then makes the whole company answer them the same way:

 - What does Meshy stand for in AI, 3D, and creative tools?

 - Why should developers, creators, game companies, and enterprise buyers care about Meshy now?

 - What is the single story that connects our product, our founders, our customers, the press, and our industry partners?

This is a founding brand role. You will write, not just direct.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN

 - Company positioning, brand architecture, core messaging, and the long-term narrative.

 - Translating hard technical capability in AI and 3D into stories that are clear, credible, and memorable.

 - One consistent voice across the website, product launches, funding announcements, founder talks, employer brand, customer stories, and sales collateral.

 - Executive narrative with the founders and leadership team: keynotes, interviews, points of view, and industry agenda-setting.

 - Major product launches and brand campaigns, from creative concept through to shipped content.

 - A reusable messaging framework that Growth, Sales, BD, PR, and Product all actually use.

 - Proof of industry impact through customer, creator, studio, and partner stories.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 8–15 years in brand strategy, brand marketing, corporate narrative, product marketing, or editorial/content strategy.

 - You have led a repositioning, category creation, or brand rebuild at a technology company—as the owner of it, not a contributor to it.

 - A portfolio we can read: website narrative, brand manifesto, a major launch, a founder keynote, or an integrated campaign.

 - You can tell a technical story to developers, creators, enterprise buyers, press, and investors—and change the register for each.

 - Exceptional English writing and editing. You personally write the things that matter most.

 - Demonstrated cross-functional influence: you’ve gotten founders, Product, Design, Marketing, and Sales to adopt one narrative and stay on it.

 - Comfortable operating as a hands-on individual contributor in an early-stage environment.


BONUS POINTS

 - Background in generative AI, creative tools, developer tools, gaming, 3D, design software, or high-growth B2B SaaS.

 - You’ve built a brand for a product whose category didn’t fully exist yet, rather than maintaining an established one.

 - You hold both technical credibility and cultural resonance—developers trust you, and the work still has emotional pull.

 - Experience taking a global or China-founded technology company into the U.S. market.

 - Founder brand, thought leadership, or executive communications experience.


THIS ROLE IS PROBABLY NOT FOR YOU IF

 - Your work is primarily PR and media relations without positioning work behind it.

 - Your background is in content marketing, SEO, social media, or community management.

 - You’re a visual creative director who owns design systems and art direction.

 - You come from consumer or lifestyle brands and haven’t worked on technical products.

About Think Zone

Think Zone is a fast-growing Bay Area learning center focused on providing personalized and effective math education for K–8 students.

We believe great education starts with great people. As we expand across the Bay Area, we're looking for motivated individuals who want to grow with us and develop their careers in education, business operations, and leadership.

About the Role

Are you a recent graduate or early in your career and looking for an opportunity where you can make an impact, develop leadership skills, and take on meaningful responsibility?

As a Learning Center Manager, you'll receive training and support to learn how to operate and grow a successful learning center. You'll work directly with students, families, tutors, and our HQ teams while gaining hands-on experience across business operations, customer experience, marketing, team leadership, and community engagement.

You don't need to come in knowing how to manage a learning center. We're looking for someone who is proactive, people-oriented, eager to learn, and excited to grow into a leadership role.

No previous management experience required. We’re looking for motivated early-career candidates who are excited to learn, take ownership, and grow into future leaders within our organization.

What You'll Learn & Do

Grow Your Center & Community

• Learn about your local community, schools, students, and families

• Build relationships with parents, schools, and community partners

• Help introduce Think Zone to more families through events, referrals, partnerships, and local outreach

• Support prospective families from their first trial class through enrollment

• Work with our Growth and Marketing teams to develop creative ideas for growing your center

Manage Center Operations

• Learn how to manage the day-to-day operations of a learning center

• Coordinate class schedules, tutors, students, and center activities

• Create a welcoming and positive experience for students and families

• Build relationships with parents and regularly gather feedback

• Help monitor student progress and ensure families receive a high level of support

Develop Your Leadership Skills

• Learn how to recruit, onboard, and support tutors with guidance from our HQ team

• Provide ongoing feedback and support to your center team

• Develop your communication, coaching, and people-management skills

• Help create a positive, energetic, and accountable center culture

Build Something From the Ground Up

Think Zone is growing, which means you'll have the opportunity to do more than simply follow an established routine.

You'll work closely with our curriculum, operations, marketing, HR, and training teams to improve processes, test new ideas, and help shape how our learning centers operate as we expand.

Who We're Looking For

You may be a great fit if you:

• Are a recent graduate or early-career professional looking for your first leadership opportunity

• Enjoy working with children, families, and people

• Are outgoing, positive, and comfortable starting conversations with new people

• Take initiative instead of waiting to be told what to do

• Enjoy solving problems and figuring things out

• Are organized, dependable, and able to manage multiple priorities

• Are excited to learn about business operations, marketing, customer experience, and team management

• Want to build a long-term career in education, operations, or leadership

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree required

• No previous management experience required

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills

• Based in the Bay Area and available for full-time, in-person work

• Mandarin proficiency is preferred but not required

• Previous experience in education, tutoring, customer service, retail, sales, student organizations, internships, or team leadership is a plus — but not required

New graduates are encouraged to apply.

Time Off & Benefits

Our learning centers have 4 scheduled shutdown weeks each year:

• July 4th Week

• Thanksgiving Week

• Christmas Week

• New Year Week

Benefits include:

• Health Insurance

• Paid Sick Leave

• 401(k) with Employer Match

• Structured Training & Mentorship

• Clear Career Advancement Path

Your Growth Path

Learning Center Manager → Regional Manager → Regional Director

This role is designed to develop future leaders within Think Zone.

You'll receive structured training, mentorship, hands-on management experience, and clear performance benchmarks as you develop your skills and take on greater responsibility.

As Think Zone continues expanding across the Bay Area, high-performing Center Managers will have opportunities to help launch additional locations and move into multi-center leadership roles.

Why Join Think Zone?

Start your leadership career early — Gain meaningful management experience without needing years of previous management experience.

Learn by doing — Build practical skills across operations, marketing, customer experience, recruiting, and people management.

Grow with the company — Join us during an expansion stage where strong performers can take on greater responsibility quickly.

Training & mentorship — You'll have support from experienced HQ teams while learning how to manage your center.

Real ownership — Bring your own ideas, experiment with new approaches, and see the direct impact of your work.

Meaningful work — Help students succeed academically while building lasting relationships with families in your community.

jobs.title: Lead Talent Acquisition Partner
jobs.description:
Make a difference with us! At Alliance Defending Freedom, we believe God has brought you here for His purpose—to stand for truth and defend the God-given right to live and speak it. Together, we protect religious freedom, free speech, the sanctity of life, marriage and family, and parental rights. Review our Statement of Faith to ensure we’re a fit for you.

Locations: Lansdowne, VA / Dallas, TX

Team Overview:

As the world's largest Christian, non-profit, legal organization, Alliance Defending Freedom depends on a Talent Acquisition function that can identify and secure mission-aligned talent at every level of the organization — from entry-level support roles to the litigation attorneys, senior leaders, and executives who carry ADF's advocacy forward. The Talent Acquisition team manages the full hiring lifecycle end to end: sourcing and screening candidates for cultural, technical, and behavioral alignment; partnering directly with Team Leaders, Senior Leadership, and the Executive Leadership Team on requisition strategy, workforce planning, and compensation decisions; and guiding every new hire through offer, background and reference checks, and onboarding.

As a Lead Talent Acquisition Partner, you will report to the Director of Talent Acquisition and will play a vital role in recruiting new hires to the organization to keep pace with ADF's continued growth and expanding global strategic footprint.

Key Responsibilities

• Own full-cycle Talent Acquisition for 15+ requisitions at a time, focused on complex roles such as litigation attorney and non-litigation attorney recruiting — sourcing, screening, interviewing, offer extension, and background/reference checks.

• Communicate with confidence and professionalism on behalf of the Talent Acquisition function, while building collaborative relationships with leaders and partners across the organization.

• Navigate a fast-growing, evolving organization with tenacity — building relationships with key stakeholders, determining how decisions get made, and advocating persuasively for candidates by clearly articulating their qualifications, expertise, and cultural, technical, and behavioral fit to support hiring, leveling, and compensation decisions.

• Understand talent needs at every level of the organization — from broad organizational priorities down to the specific needs of an individual team — and match candidates strategically to meet those needs, going beyond simply filling an open requisition.

• Serve as a trusted advisor throughout the hiring process by designing thoughtful, role-specific interview questions for each candidate and search, and gathering the insight needed to form a well-supported view of a candidate's technical, behavioral, and cultural fit.

• Deliver excellent candidate interview experiences for the organization's most complex and highest-visibility searches.

• Maintain accurate, up-to-date candidate and requisition records in Greenhouse, including interview scorecards and disposition status.

• Lead compensation negotiations for assigned requisitions in line with internal budgets, ensuring competitive offers and candidate satisfaction.

• Proactively expand and promote ADF's Talent Acquisition brand through professional networks, events, and outreach channels.

• Continuously seek ways to improve Talent Acquisition processes, utilize technology for efficiency, and enhance the candidate experience.

• Mentor and assist other Talent Acquisition team members, including sharing sourcing initiatives, interviewing techniques, and process knowledge.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Business, Communications, Human Resources Management, or a related field.

• 6+ years of full life-cycle recruiting experience, including experience recruiting for senior leadership and specialized roles, such as legal, niche technical positions, or other hard-to-fill roles.

• Proficient in Applicant Tracking Systems (e.g., Greenhouse, Workday, Ashby) for maintaining accurate, well-organized candidate and requisition records.

• Skilled in sourcing strategies and pipeline-building for hard-to-fill and recurring specialized roles.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication, including confident, persuasive communication with senior stakeholders.

• Ability to navigate a fast-growing, evolving organization with tenacity, sound judgment, and resourcefulness.

Preferred Qualifications

• 8+ years of full life-cycle recruiting experience.

• 2+ years of legal, executive, and/or staffing agency recruiting experience.

• Experience with Greenhouse

Pay & Benefits

At Alliance Defending Freedom, we offer a competitive compensation and benefits package to support your well-being and growth. While we do not disclose specific salary ranges, our compensation is competitive with top non-profit law firms. Our benefits include 100% covered medical and dental insurance, medical and dependent care reimbursement, paid disability, long-term care, life insurance, and a 401(k) plan with a 4% company match. We prioritize work-life balance with paid time off and 12 paid holidays each year.

Want to Know More About ADF?

This salary range is reflective of a position based in Lansdowne, VA. This range is a good-faith estimate, and the actual salary may vary based on the candidate’s experience, skills, qualifications, and office location.

Virginia Salary Range

Why Choose Cortica?

Here’s what makes us different:

What Makes Cortica Different from Other ABA Companies?

• Transdisciplinary Approach: Work alongside experts in occupational therapy, speech-language therapy, pediatrics, and more—because we care for the whole child.

Be part of a team that’s redefining ABA therapy with compassion, innovation, and collaboration.

Ready to make a difference? Apply today!
